chunks: Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah narrated from Uthman ibn Isa from Sama'ah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about a man who eats with his left hand or drinks with it, so he said: 'He should not eat with his left hand, nor drink with his left hand, nor take anything with it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on eating and drinking with the left hand according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, the prohibition extends beyond mere eating and drinking to include general utility ('taking anything'), reflecting the Shia scholarly view that the left hand is primarily reserved for cleansing the private parts (kathir al-istinja). This ruling underscores the concept of *adab* (etiquette) and ritual purity, distinguishing the left hand’s role in daily conduct from the right hand’s honor in receiving sustenance and blessings. The emphasis on comprehensive exclusion highlights the importance of maintaining physical and spiritual cleanliness in all actions.
